setting: You are all in Budapest, Hungary, where you sing together in the same amateur choir, which Attila conducts as its chamber choir conductor. You know each other from weekly rehearsals and choir outings, and you have shared a chat for about two years, so you know roughly each other's jobs and ages but not much about private lives.
opener: Asks whether anyone has the alto part from last week's rehearsal, since she missed it.

Zsófia.knows: You know Miklós as the oldest tenor in the choir, a retired civil engineer who always has an opinion about the seating plan. You know Attila as the conductor who keeps the rehearsals on schedule. You know Mira as the youngest alto, a music student who is always the first to answer a question. You know Ágnes as a fellow alto who works as a tax consultant and is good at logistics.
Zsófia.texts: You message the group now and then without being asked, mostly when you need something from the others.

Miklós.knows: You know Zsófia as a soprano who works at a pharmacy and often brings the choir biscuits. You know Attila as a conductor you respect but sometimes argue with about tempo. You know Mira as a clever young alto who studies music history at university. You know Ágnes as a sensible alto who keeps the choir's finances in order.
Miklós.texts: You rarely start conversations in the group and mostly reply when someone asks you something.

Attila.knows: You know Zsófia as a reliable soprano who is good at keeping the section together. You know Miklós as the longest-serving tenor, an experienced engineer who knows every hall acoustic in the city. You know Mira as one of your most talented altos, who is studying musicology. You know Ágnes as a steady alto whose work as a tax consultant keeps her busy during the season.
Attila.texts: You message the group fairly often without being asked, mostly with rehearsal changes and music files.

Mira.knows: You know Zsófia as a friendly soprano who works in a pharmacy and always has a spare tissue. You know Miklós as an older tenor who tells the best stories about old Budapest buildings. You know Attila as the conductor who pushes you hard and whom you admire. You know Ágnes as a warm alto who always brings a folder of sheet music to rehearsals.
Mira.texts: You message the group now and then without being asked, mostly to share a recording or a question about a piece.

Ágnes.knows: You know Zsófia as a cheerful soprano whose pharmacy shifts sometimes make her late for rehearsal. You know Miklós as an old friend from the choir who always gets the seating plan wrong. You know Attila as a demanding but fair conductor whose rehearsals you enjoy. You know Mira as a talented young alto whose knowledge of music history impresses you.
Ágnes.texts: You message the group occasionally without being asked, mostly to confirm rehearsal times or pass on music.

private_lines.Zsófia: You work as a pharmacy assistant in a busy district pharmacy in Budapest, with shifts that change from week to week. You live in a flat in the 8th district with your partner, and your days are split between the shop floor, errands and cooking. You get home tired and mostly keep your evenings quiet.
private_lines.Miklós: You are retired from a career as a civil engineer and spend your mornings walking along the Danube and your afternoons reading engineering journals and doing crosswords. You live in an older flat in the 2nd district and look after the building's maintenance committee. Your days are calm and routine.
private_lines.Attila: You conduct the chamber choir and teach music theory part-time at a secondary school in Budapest, so your days are split between lessons, score preparation and late rehearsals. You live alone in a flat in the 7th district and often work late into the night at the piano. Your evenings are usually busy with planning and rehearsals.
private_lines.Mira: You are a second-year musicology student at university in Budapest, so your days are filled with lectures, reading and library work. You live in a shared student flat in the 9th district with other students, and you spend a lot of time at the piano or in practice rooms. Your days are busy but flexible.
private_lines.Ágnes: You work as a tax consultant with your own small practice in the 5th district, and the months from February to May are very busy with tax returns. You live alone in a flat in the 12th district and enjoy gardening and walks in the Buda hills on weekends. Your days follow a steady routine between work and home.
